summary: The hypothesis that multi-start simulated annealing (SA) with greedy local search would vastly outperform the baseline on Max-Cut is confirmed. The SA solution scored 84.62 out of 100, up from 0 (unimplemented stub) and far above the ~51 expected from random assignment. This falls slightly below the predicted ≥85 threshold and the designer's probe score of 87.28, likely due to per-test-case variance.
key_points: SA treatment scored 84.62 vs 0 (stub baseline) and ~51 (random baseline) — a massive improvement confirming the directional hypothesis.

The score of 84.62 is slightly below the designer's earlier probe of 87.28 and the predicted ≥85, suggesting room for further tuning (e.g., more restarts, longer annealing schedule, or switching to a stronger local search like Kernighan-Lin style moves).

The algorithm uses 20 random restarts with greedy + SA (T=3.0, alpha=0.99997) and a post-SA greedy refinement pass; the ~2.7-point gap to the probe suggests gains may come from better time allocation, adaptive perturbation sizes, or a dedicated 1-flip local search hill climb.
No format or correctness issues were observed; the solution compiles, runs within time limits, and produces valid output on all test cases.
